author: jsign
content:
yep, you're not missing anything. With a real parent every node is reached by hash from the canonical state root, so reaching a malformed one would need a keccak collision... so all this effort is just trying to be more paranoid about stuff, so can be argued if this happens we have bigger problems. but  the logic is to be conservative.

so, these tests only cover hand-built parents in tests. The guest only sees the input bytes and can't tell the difference, so the fixtures define what the result should be when the block reads through a malformed node. Malformed nodes that the block doesn't reach aren't tested, so adding structural checks when loading the witness is fine to pass them (checking lazily works too).

(A bit more details on how all this convo unfolded here https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/1451216716062523507/1562757196570169386)
